fields.meta_description: Build a benefits enrollment form for new hires, open enrollment, and life events, and keep every election in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Benefits Enrollment Form for Every Enrollment Window
fields.hero_description: Build a benefits enrollment form where employees compare plans and add dependents, with every election stored in tables you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Handles Before HR Has To
fields.features_subheading: Describe your plans and enrollment rules. Emergent builds the form employees fill in, the deadlines behind it, and the tables HR reads.
fields.feature_1:
Plans side by side, priced per paycheck

Show each medical plan with its deductible and the employee's cost per paycheck. Switching the tier from employee only to family reprices every plan on the same screen.
fields.feature_2:
A row for each person covered

Add a spouse or child with name, relationship, and date of birth. Each dependent is tied to the plans they join. Dental can cover the kids while medical covers one adult.
fields.feature_3:
Deadlines counted from the right date

The app counts each window from the employee's start date or event date and closes it when the days run out. Reminder emails go out 7 days and 2 days before the end.
fields.feature_4:
Waivers with the reason on file

An employee who declines coverage picks a reason, names the other plan if there is one, and signs. The waiver lands in the same table as an election, under the same employee.
fields.feature_5:
Every election in a table you own

Elections save to a database you own, one row per employee and plan. The HR dashboard shows who has finished and who has waived, plus how many days each open form has left.
fields.feature_6:
The whole form, exported to GitHub

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and run it next to your HR systems. Keep changing the form by prompt after export, or edit the code by hand.

fields.usecase_heading: One Form for Every Time Someone Enrolls
fields.tab_content_1:
Gareth picks Silver PPO for two on day 4 of 30

Dorrance Millwork gives each new hire 30 days to enroll. On day 4, Gareth Linwood compares 3 medical plans for employee and spouse: Bronze HDHP at $38, Silver PPO at $96, and Gold PPO at $151 a paycheck. He takes Silver PPO and dental, not vision. The elections save to the HR table with 26 days to spare.
fields.tab_content_2:
All but 28 of 140 staff enroll by day 11

Aldergrove Animal Hospital opens enrollment for 14 days each fall, and every form starts with last year's elections filled in. By day 11, 112 of the 140 staff have submitted. The other 28 get an email reminder with their own link, and Yesenia Dunleavy in HR watches the count on her dashboard.
fields.tab_content_3:
From the day he was born, Bogdan's son is covered

Bogdan Truett opens the form at Tuckahoe Brewing 9 days after his son is born. He picks Birth as the event and adds his son to medical and dental. The form shows 21 days left of the 30 days he has to notify the plan, and HR gets the request by email when he submits. His son's coverage starts on the date of birth.
fields.tab_content_4:
Pilar's medical waiver is signed and on file

Pilar Kaskade is covered on her spouse's plan, so she waives medical at Baylock Bakery and keeps dental. The waiver asks for her reason and the other plan's carrier, Wenlock Health, then her signature. It saves under her employee record, and the HR table now shows 9 of Baylock's 46 staff with a signed waiver.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Benefits Enrollment Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a benefits enrollment form that prices each plan by tier and tracks every deadline, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List every plan and its price
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide who can enroll, and when
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for the employee, then the tier
fields.howto_step_1_des: Put every plan you offer in one sheet with the employee cost per paycheck for every coverage tier, from employee only up to family. The form reads its prices from this sheet. A new rate next year is then one edit.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down the windows your plans use: the new hire period, the open enrollment dates, and the life events that reopen enrollment. Confirm each window and its start date with your plan administrator before you build, because the form will close on those days.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Start with who the employee is, then ask for the coverage tier. Show the plans only after the tier is set. Every price on screen is then the one the employee will pay. Keep each benefit as its own choice, with its own plans and its own waive option.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask once for each spouse or child, with the details your carriers need. Then let the employee tick which plans each person joins. A child can sit on dental without joining medical, and nobody types the same person twice on one form.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Give waivers a reason and a signature
fields.howto_step_5_des: Offer a waiver for each benefit an employee declines. Ask for the reason and, when they are covered elsewhere, the other plan's carrier. Capture a signature at the end and keep the waiver with the rest of that employee's record.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Choose who hears about each change
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send each new election and life event to HR by email, and send the employee a copy of what they chose. The morning after a window ends, give HR a list of anyone whose form is still open, with their manager's name beside it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it with three made-up employees
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the form to Emergent and fill it in as a new hire with a spouse, a parent adding a newborn, and someone who waives medical. Check that the HR table shows each election at the right price before you publish the form.

faq_plan.q: What is a benefits enrollment form?
faq_plan.a: A benefits enrollment form records which plans an employee joins or declines, and at which coverage tier. It also lists the dependents on each plan. HR uses the completed form to set up coverage with each carrier and the matching deductions.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a benefits enrollment form?
faq_plan.a: Describe your plans, the price of each coverage tier, and your enrollment windows to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form and its deadline logic, along with the HR table behind it. Fill it in as a few made-up employees, adjust anything by prompt, and publish once every election lands at the right price.

faq_plan.q: Is a benefits enrollment form template enough for open enrollment?
faq_plan.a: No, not once the form has to price plans and track deadlines. A fixed template collects choices, and HR checks prices and deadlines by hand. A form built from your own plan list can price each tier and start from last year's elections. Emergent builds that version from a prompt, with no cap on responses.

faq_plan.q: What information should a benefits enrollment form ask for?
faq_plan.hint: How to fill out a benefits enrollment form?
faq_plan.a: Plan for four groups: the employee's name, ID, and start date; the coverage tier; a plan or a waiver per benefit; and the details of each dependent. Keep bank details for pay off this form and on a separate direct deposit form.

faq_plan.q: How long should a benefits enrollment form stay open for new hires?
faq_plan.a: Your plan sets the window, so build the form to close on the day your plan documents give. One federal limit applies to when coverage starts: a group health plan may not use a waiting period that exceeds 90 days. Count each new hire's window from their own start date.

faq_plan.q: Can a benefits enrollment form handle changes after a life event?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Under the Department of Labor's guidance, after a birth, adoption, or placement for adoption, the employee must notify the plan within 30 days. A newly married employee requests enrollment within 30 days after the marriage. Count those days from the event date the employee enters.

faq_plan.q: How does a benefits enrollment form connect to payroll deductions?
faq_plan.a: Each election carries a cost per paycheck, and that amount becomes the deduction. The app can send finished elections to your payroll tool through its API, or HR can enter them. Other pay changes, such as a new rate or tax withholding, belong on a payroll change form.

faq_plan.q: Should a benefits enrollment form let employees waive coverage?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A waive option on each benefit lets an employee decline medical and still join dental. Ask for a signature on every waiver. It shows HR the choice was deliberate and not a missed form, and it gives HR one record to check if that employee later asks to join mid-year.

faq_plan.q: Can one benefits enrollment form cover medical, dental, and vision?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each benefit its own plans, prices, and waive option on the same form, and let the tier differ by benefit. One submission then holds every election for that employee. With Emergent, those elections live in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a benefits enrollment form easy to finish on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Show one question per screen, label every field in plain words, and let employees save and come back before the deadline. Emergent can build the form as a one-question-per-screen flow. Link a reasonable accommodation request form from the first screen for anyone who needs another way to enroll.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Benefits Enrollment Form for Every Enrollment Window'; hero 'Build a benefits enrollment form where employees compare plans and add dependents, with every election stored in tables you own.' covers the whole job (plans, dependents, elections), under 130 chars.

intent.evidence: Informational searchers get what the form asks for (FAQ 4 'Plan for four groups...'), the template question (FAQ 3), windows and life events (FAQ 5-6) and a seven-step build.

specificity.evidence: HR vocabulary throughout: 'cost per paycheck', 'coverage tier', 'Bronze HDHP at $38', 'waive option', 'plan administrator'.

openers.evidence: Feature bodies open on verbs or full sentences: 'Show each medical plan...', 'Add a spouse or child...', 'An employee who declines coverage picks a reason...'.

craft.evidence: Varied sentences, one idea each: 'He takes Silver PPO and dental, not vision. The elections save to the HR table with 26 days to spare.' Two ', so' endings, under the limit.

voice.evidence: Concrete, unglamorous details: 'Baylock Bakery', '9 of Baylock's 46 staff with a signed waiver', 'with their manager's name beside it'. No hype.

truth.evidence: DOL quotes checked against the publication text: 'you must notify the plan within 30 days ... of the birth, adoption, or placement for adoption', 'The child's coverage will be effective on the date of the birth', 'within 30 days after you marry'; TR 12-02 90-day waiting period. Numbers agree: 112+28=140, day 4 + 26 = 30, 9 + 21 = 30, 7+2 = 9 waivers. Claims map to claims_used.

distinct.evidence: Own stories (new hire, open enrollment, birth, waiver); sibling primaries appear only as FAQ link anchors ('payroll change form', 'direct deposit form', 'reasonable accommodation request form'), never as headings.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic builder questions, answer-first ('Yes. A waive option on each benefit...'); hub link in item 2; secondary 'benefits enrollment form template' in item 3; paa --spec 10 pass, 0 reject, 0 flag.

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches tab copy: '$38/$96/$151', 'Day 4 of 30 / 26 days to spare', '112 of 140 submitted', 'Reminder sent to 28 staff', '21 days left', '9 of 46'. One hero per panel, readable.

findings.quote: Reminder emails go out 7 days and 2 days before the end.
findings.issue: Feature 3 states a fixed reminder schedule (7 and 2 days before), while tab 2 and its mockup remind at day 11 of 14 ('Three days before it closes'). Different employers can configure this, but a reader sees two schedules.
findings.fix: Phrase feature 3 as a configurable example ('for example 7 days and 2 days before') or align tab 2 to one of those offsets.

findings.quote: adds his son to medical and dental ... His son's coverage starts on the date of birth.
findings.issue: The DOL source ties the 30-day notice and date-of-birth effective date to HIPAA special enrollment in an employer health plan; dental is not clearly covered by it, and the tab applies it to both.
findings.fix: Say 'His son's medical coverage starts on the date of birth' to keep the source's scope.

findings.quote: pick dental and vision, and sign before their 30-day window closes.
